response.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT m.department, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM income i JOIN member me ON i.link_to_member = me.member_id JOIN major m ON me.link_to_major = m.major_id GROUP BY m.department), s AS (SELECT department, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM d), a AS (SELECT *, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Each income row linked to a member who has a major counts once. Income rows with no matching member or major are dropped (inner joins). Departments with no such incomes are not included in the average share.
Departments are grouped by the major.department text value. Different majors in the same department are combined.
